paragraph: Angola's submarine cables land in Luanda at two stations, [Sangano and Cacuaco, Angola Telecom said in July 2026](<https://pti.ao/angola-telecom-preve-operacao-do-cabo-submarino-sarssy-ate-2027/>). [Angola Cables runs the Sangano station for SACS](<https://theconversation.com/undersea-cables-for-africas-internet-retrace-history-225912>), which [has joined Luanda to Fortaleza in Brazil since 2018](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/soberania-digital-do-governo-de-angola-uma-necessidade-que-se-impoe/>). In the last twelve months, [Unitel opened its 2Africa landing station at Cacuaco in December 2025](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/unitel-invete-mais-de-40-milhoes-de-dolares-americano-em-fibra-optica/>). [Angola Telecom also reported a fibre link from Santa Clara to Ondjiva in Namibia](<https://pti.ao/angola-telecom-preve-operacao-do-cabo-submarino-sarssy-ate-2027/>), carrying both countries' operators' services. In September 2026 Ciena said [Angola Cables sells wholesale capacity on SACS and its MONET cable](<https://www.ciena.com/about/newsroom/press-releases/angola-cables-boosts-capacity-across-monet-and-sacs-submarine-cable-systems-with-ciena-technology>).

[In July 2021 the regulator ARCT said Burundi reaches the EASSy, SEACOM and TEAMS cables through its neighbours](<https://arct.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/RAPPORT-SUR-LES-INDICATEURS-TIC-2020-VERSION-PUBLIE.pdf>). [It lists two fibre crossings each with Rwanda, the DRC and Tanzania](<https://arct.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/RAPPORT-SUR-LES-INDICATEURS-TIC-2020-VERSION-PUBLIE.pdf>). [Burundi Backbone System joins Tanzania's backbone at Kabanga and Manyovu, under a contract renewed in February 2024](<https://www.ttcl.co.tz/sw/blog-details/sw/ttcl-yazidi-kujikita-kimataifa-kibiashara>). In the last twelve months, [TTCL and Burundi Backbone System agreed in September 2026 to raise that link from 4 Gbps to 10 Gbps](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/09/ttcl-bbs-increase-tanzania-burundi-connectivity-capacity-10gbps/>). No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries Burundi's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic.

[The deal record states Maroc Telecom's West Africa submarine cable lands at Cotonou](<https://medias24.com/2023/06/01/150-millions-deuros-pour-le-west-africa-cable-sous-marin-a-fibre-optique-de-maroc-telecom/>). [Its south segment was operational in July 2021](<https://medias24.com/2023/06/01/150-millions-deuros-pour-le-west-africa-cable-sous-marin-a-fibre-optique-de-maroc-telecom/>). In the last twelve months, [Mobile Europe reported on 15 July 2026 that CSquared's architecture includes the Equiano cable, landing in Nigeria and Togo](<https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/csquared-boosts-internet-resilence-integrating-with-2africa-west/>). It says the cable reaches Benin by terrestrial backbone. No source found says other operators buy capacity at the landing station or on the routes, or that they run on open-access or wholesale terms. Mature would need other operators to buy capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable to run on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[Maroc Telecom's 5,700 km transafrican terrestrial fibre cable runs from Morocco to Niger via Mauritania, Mali and Burkina Faso](<https://leseco.ma/business/maroc-telecom-plus-de-454-mmdh-investis-en-afrique.html>). The record gives 2022 as its year of completion. In the last twelve months, [Agence Ecofin said on 17 August 2026 that Burkina Faso relies on Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana and Togo for submarine-cable capacity](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/1708-140913-le-burkina-faso-se-tourne-vers-le-nigeria-pour-son-acces-a-la-connectivite-internationale>). [Mobile Europe said on 15 July 2026 that Equiano reaches the country over CSquared's terrestrial backbone](<https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/csquared-boosts-internet-resilence-integrating-with-2africa-west/>). No source found says other operators buy capacity on these routes, or that they run on open-access or wholesale terms. Mature would need other operators to buy capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable to run on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[BoFiNet counts three international submarine cable systems for Botswana: EASSy, WACS and Equiano](<https://www.bofinet.co.bw/uploads/571/01M07F2TQ2HE6M06GD31SSDFZG.pdf>), in its report to March 2025. [Paratus Botswana opened its 840 km Kalahari fibre on 29 May 2024](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/79822>). It completed a route to Equiano at Swakopmund in Namibia. In the last twelve months, [BoFiNet raised its capacity through two crossings into South Africa from 300 Gbit/s to 1 Tbit/s in September 2026](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/fiber-networking/bofinet-upgrades-its-available-international-capacity-to-1tbit-s>). No source found says other operators buy capacity at the landing station or on the cable. Mature would need other operators buying capacity on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[Agence Ecofin said on 12 October 2026 that the Central African Republic has two terrestrial fibre links to neighbours, through Cameroon and through Congo-Brazzaville](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/1210-142321-internet-qu-est-ce-que-la-liaison-par-fibre-avec-la-rdc-peut-apporter-a-la-centrafrique>). They run on the Central African Backbone, about 935 km of fibre. In the last twelve months, [a ministry official said on 30 August 2026 that the planned Congo-Brazzaville interconnection remains to be realised](<https://www.camerounlink.com/news/2026/9/1/acces-aux-cables-sous-marins-quelles-options-pour-la-centrafrique-au-dela-du-cameroun-156491/>). No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable to carry the country's traffic.

[Five submarine cables land at Abidjan](<https://www.africabandwidthmaps.com/?p=7464>), the regulator ARTCI reported: SAT-3, ACE, WACS, MainOne and Maroc Telecom's West Africa cable. [Developing Telecoms counts six, with 2Africa](<https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/optical-fixed-networks/17258-guinea-adds-cote-d-ivoire-to-regional-fibre-interconnectivity-plan.html>). [MainOne's branch landed at Grand Bassam, near Abidjan, and entered service in December 2019](<https://www.submarinenetworks.com/en/systems/euro-africa/mainone/mainone-cable-branch-to-cote-d-ivoire-ready-for-service>). In the last twelve months, [the 2Africa branch was back in service at the end of July 2026](<https://subseacables.blogspot.com/2026/08/2africa-ivory-coast-branch-live-again.html>), after two days of outages. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes that share no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[A 2024 report of the regulator ART, quoted by Ecomatin, says Camtel has three landing stations, at Kribi, Limbe and Douala, for the SAT3, WACS, NCSCS and SAIL cables](<https://ecomatin.net/cameroun-camtel-a-gagne-34-milliards-fcfa-grace-a-la-fibre-optique-en-2024-en-hausse-de-17>). [The same report says Camtel's capacity lets it sell international transmission to national and sub-regional operators](<https://ecomatin.net/cameroun-camtel-a-gagne-34-milliards-fcfa-grace-a-la-fibre-optique-en-2024-en-hausse-de-17>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries Cameroon's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic, beside the routes already in service.

[WACS and 2Africa both land at Muanda on the Atlantic coast](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1210-59658-central-african-republic-revives-talks-on-third-internet-route-via-drc>), Ecofin reported. [WACS was connected in 2013, and 2Africa landed in September 2023](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0305-138080-la-rdc-veut-renforcer-ses-moyens-de-connectivite-internet-internationale>). In the last twelve months, [2Africa went live in December 2025](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/wacs-submarine-cable-outage-disrupts-drc-internet-access>), and [Airtel put it into service with 200 Gbps on 18 December 2025](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/airteldrc_airtel-congo-rdc-sa-1er-r%C3%A9seau-%C3%A0-mettre-activity-7407828782549655552-0p5z>). [Paratus switched on its 2,000 km G2M fibre from Goma to Mombasa on 9 February 2026](<https://itweb.africa/article/paratus-lights-up-new-east-africa-fibre-highway-linking-goma-to-mombasa/wbrpOqg2aJQMDLZn>), and says it carries traffic for its first wholesale customers. [The WACS segment between the DRC and Congo was back in service on 16 November 2026 after repairs](<https://www.itweb.africa/article/wacs-subsea-cable-returns-online/lLn147mQ96Z7J6Aa>).

[Congo has been on the WACS cable since 2012](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/congo-wants-to-connect-to-new-cable-amidst-wacs-failures>), and [the President activated the 2Africa connection at Pointe-Noire on 28 February 2024](<https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/republic-of-congo-launches-data-center-in-pointe-noire-for-2africa-cable>). [The minister said in May 2025 that Congo is linked by fibre to five neighbours](<https://labreveonline.com/osiane-le-congo-et-5-pays-voisins-desormais-interconnectes-par-fibre-optique/>). In the last twelve months, [a cut on 2 January 2026 took out WACS, then the main international link](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/arpce-congo_arpcecongo-internet-communications-activity-7430183167946395649-Nhfl>). [WACS was repaired on 12 February 2026](<https://www.arpce.cg/actualites/apres-la-panne-du-wacs-les-operateurs-congolais-renforcent-leur-connectivite-grace-au-cable-2africa/>). [A further fault on 29 October 2026 sent Congo Telecom's traffic to backup links](<https://itweb.africa/article/wacs-cable-repairs-enter-critical-phase/lLn14MmQ9DnMJ6Aa>). Mature would need other operators buying capacity on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[Digital Watch Observatory states Comoros is linked to regional and global fibre systems including EASSy, FLY-LION3 and 2Africa](<http://web.archive.org/web/20260824175002/https://dig.watch/countries/comoros>). [The Comorian minister said 2Africa will be a fourth international submarine cable joining those already operational](<https://pp.itu.int/2022/en/itu_policy_statements/kamalidini-souef-comoros/>). [Comores Câbles states on an undated page that 2Africa has been put into service](<https://www.comorescables.km/Technologies>). [Huawei Marine announced it delivered the 260 km Avassa submarine cable between Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mayotte](<https://www.huawei.com/en/news/2016/11/avassa-submarine-cable-project>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes that share no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[Caboverde24, citing Cabo Verde Telecom, reported in September 2026 that WACS, EllaLink and SHARE currently reach Praia](<https://caboverde24.info/2026/09/08/cvtelecom-leva-a-lisboa-ambicao-de-transformar-cabo-verde-num-hub-digital-do-atlantico/>), with direct routes to Lisbon, West Africa and Fortaleza in Brazil. All three land at Praia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says other operators buy capacity on these routes, or that they run on open-access or wholesale terms. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes that share no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[Djibouti Telecom runs two landing stations, YAC A and Haramous](<https://www.submarinenetworks.com/en/nv/news/djibouti-telecom-builds-a-new-cable-landing-station-in-djibouti-city>), with eight submarine systems between them. [Djibouti Telecom says its cable stations serve more than 50 telecom operators](<https://magazinedelafrique.com/african-business/vers-un-hub-numerique-mondial/>), African Business reported in May 2024. In the last twelve months, [the prime minister put the number of cables landing in Djibouti at 14 in March 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/djibouti-echange-avec-huawei-sur-le-developpement-de-ses-infrastructures-numeriques>). [La Nation said in January 2026 that Djibouti Telecom holds the monopoly of international telecoms](<https://www.lanation.dj/du-hub-regional-au-catalyseur-continental-la-nouvelle-ere-de-djibouti-telecom/>). [The finance minister said in September 2026 that twelve cables land in Djibouti](<https://sonna.so/en/article/Somali-must-have-a-place-in-artificial-intelligence-Djibouti-minister-tells-first-national-forum>). No source found says capacity is sold on regulated wholesale terms.

[Algeria is connected through four submarine cable systems](<http://news.radioalgerie.dz/fr/node/77708>), the minister told parliament in January 2026. [Algerie Telecom's 2024 deck places them at three coastal cities](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Regional-Presence/ArabStates/Documents/events/2024/MeaningfulConnectivity/Presentations/Session6/Evolution%20de%20Infrastructure%20de%20Transport%20Ip%20Final-Mounira.pdf>): Oran and Algiers for the cables to Spain, Annaba for SEA-ME-WE 4. In the last twelve months, [traffic moved to other cables during maintenance on the Algeria-Spain cable in October 2026](<https://algerie-eco.com/2026/10/27/internet-retour-a-la-normale-apres-la-maintenance-du-cable-sous-marin-reliant-lalgerie-et-lespagne/>), and service returned to normal on 27 October. No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic.

[Telecom Egypt operates 10 landing stations on the Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts, among them Alexandria, Port Said, Ras Ghareb, Suez and Zafarana](<https://te.eg/interactivemap/assets/downloads/Telecom_Egypt_The_Digital_Hub.pdf>). [2Africa lands at Ras Ghareb and Port Said, Telecom Egypt said in November 2025](<https://ir.te.eg/en/CorporateNews/PressRelease/232/The-Completion-of-2Africa-A-Consortium-Milestone-for-Global-Connectivity>). [It completed SEA-ME-WE-6 landings at the same two stations in July 2025](<https://capacityglobal.com/news/telecom-egypt-5pbs-red-sea-bypass/>). [Telecom Egypt runs WeConnect, an open and neutral platform for cross-connecting the cable systems at its landing stations](<https://te.eg/interactivemap/assets/downloads/Telecom_Egypt_The_Digital_Hub.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [the minister said in September 2026 that 20 international subsea cables cross Egypt](<https://itmagazineme.com/egypt-allocates-440000-consultancy-budget-to-draft-national-data-centre-strategy/>), carrying 90% of internet traffic between Europe and Asia.

[In August 2026 Mesob Journal said Eritrea is the only coastal African state without an operational submarine cable landing station](<https://mesobjournal.com/post/eritrea-digital-sovereignty-red-sea-internet-gateway>). The same piece proposes a landing at Massawa or Assab and an exchange point in Asmara. [In June 2024 Middle East Eye reported cable firms looking at Eritrea's waters as a route avoiding Yemen](<https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/cable-firms-eye-eritrea-yemen-houthi-attacks-threaten-internet-traffic>), and that the government did not reply to their requests. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a land link abroad, or says there is none. Preparing would need one fibre route to carry the country's internet traffic abroad: a submarine cable landing in the country, or a fibre link through a neighbour.

[La Nation's profile of Djibouti Telecom lists a terrestrial cable between Djibouti and Ethiopia in the operator's network](<https://www.lanation.dj/du-hub-regional-au-catalyseur-continental-la-nouvelle-ere-de-djibouti-telecom/>), linking Ethiopia to Djibouti's submarine cable landings. This is the one international fibre route found in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a second international fibre route in service. Nothing has been found saying other operators buy capacity on this route, or that it runs on open-access or wholesale terms. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one that shares a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[TM Africa said in September 2026 that Gabon lands four subsea cable systems: 2Africa, ACE, Maroc Telecom's West Africa cable and SAT-3/WASC](<https://tmafrica.co.ug/news/gabon-builds-digital-state-shrinking-oil-base>). [ACE Gabon operates the Libreville landing station](<https://spin.ga/nos-activites/ace-gabon/>). In the last twelve months, [full ACE service was restored on 4 June 2026 after a fault on 27-28 May](<https://axionegabon.com/details-d-actualite/communique-incident-sur-cable-sous-marin-ace>). [In October 2026 SPIN's director-general said the national backbone links Gabon physically with Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and Congo](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-numerique-interview-bertrand-mahoukou-bitchinda-expose-la-strategie-de-la-spin-pour-etendre-la-fibre-optique/>). He said cross-border traffic stays low. No source found says other operators buy capacity at the Libreville landing or on the land links. Mature would need other operators buying capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[Ghana's regulator counts five submarine cable providers](<https://nca.org.gh/submarine-cable-landing/>): SAT-3, MainOne, WACS, Glo and ACE. In the last twelve months, [2Africa was activated in late 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/02/12/2africa-is-here-how-africa-can-capture-the-full-potential-of-the-subsea-cable/>), with MTN's Bayobab leading its landing in Ghana. [CSquared said in July 2026 that its backbone carries Ghana's traffic to Equiano](<https://csquared.com/csquared-adds-2africa-west-capacity-to-strengthen-regional-internet-resilience/>), which lands in Nigeria and Togo. [The regulator's November 2024 authorisation template lets its holder provide capacity on a submarine cable to licensed operators](<https://nca.org.gh/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Electronic-Communication-Submarine-Carrier-Services-Authorisation_November-2024-V5.pdf>). The template names no holder and no cable. Mature would need other operators buying capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[The ACE consortium says ACE landed at Conakry as Guinea's first international cable and entered service on 15 December 2012](<https://ace-submarinecable.com/en/submarine-cable/>). In the last twelve months, [the Medusa cable was signed in May 2026 to be Guinea's second](<https://medusascs.com/news/guinea-seals-its-alliance-with-medusa-submarine-cable-system-for-a-second-submarine-cable/>). [On 27 October 2026 the ministry's secretary general told MPs that Guinea depends on a single submarine cable, close to saturation](<https://mediaguinee.com/2026/10/loi-de-finances-rectificative-medias-publics-en-difficulte-et-risques-de-coupure-dinternet-au-coeur-des-echanges-avec-les-deputes/>). [Actu7 wrote in August 2026 that the Medusa link is not yet in service](<https://actu7.com/index.php/fibre-cables-et-medias-les-grands-defis-de-mourana-soumah/>). No source found names a second international fibre route in service, by sea or through a neighbour. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[GAMTEL states two international routes in service: the ACE cable, and a 28 Gbps backup link with Free in Senegal](<https://gamtel.gm/about-us/>). [It says traffic is rerouted automatically to the backup if ACE fails](<https://gamtel.gm/about-us/>). In the last twelve months, [the ACE cable station at Sukuta lost power on 4 June 2026, causing a nationwide outage, The Point reported](<https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/headlines/nation-hit-by-internet-outage-amid-ongoing-power-cuts>). [TechGriot wrote in September 2026 that The Gambia remains dependent on a single undersea cable, with terrestrial redundancy through Senegal still thin](<https://techgriot.co/english/africa/2026/09/senegal-and-gambias-digital-deal-is-really-about-cables-and-spectrum/>). No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic.

[Guinea-Bissau joined its first international submarine cable, ACE, in March 2023](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2908-131059-deploiement-de-la-fibre-optique-la-guinee-bissau-veut-apprendre-du-tchad>). [Agence Ecofin says the country's international connectivity is confined to the coast](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2908-131059-deploiement-de-la-fibre-optique-la-guinee-bissau-veut-apprendre-du-tchad>). [In June 2024 ECOWAS said the six countries of its Amilcar Cabral cable project, Guinea-Bissau among them, each have one landing station](<https://www.ecowas.int/4th-meeting-of-the-ecowas-ministerial-steering-committee-for-the-amilcar-cabral-submarine-telecom-cable-project/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a second international fibre route in service. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[Ceiba-2, a 400 km cable linking Malabo, Bata and Kribi in Cameroon, was inaugurated on 4 June 2018 beside the ACE cable](<https://afr-ix.com/equatorial-guinea-and-cameroon-are-now-more-connected/>). [On 10 November 2025 the national backbones of Gabon and Equatorial Guinea were joined at Meyo-Kyé and Ebebeyin](<https://spin.ga/alliance-historique-numerique-gabon-guinee-equatoriale/>). In the last twelve months, [Ecofin said in October 2026 that the country still relies mainly on the ACE cable](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2110-59971-equatorial-guinea-service-quality-a-priority-for-new-telecom-operator-telgesa>). [GITGE's annual report, from about 2016, says it sells capacity to ISPs and government companies on open, non-discriminatory terms](<https://gitge.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/PRESENTACION-6.pdf>). No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable to carry the country's traffic.

[The Communications Authority's June 2026 figures put Kenya's international bandwidth at 28,950 Gbps over seven cable systems](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/09/19/kenya-fixed-internet-fibre-wireless-satellite-growth/>). They are SEACOM, TEAMS, EASSy, Lion2, DARE1, PEACE and 2Africa, all landing at Mombasa. In the last twelve months, Seacom opened a Nairobi-Kisumu-Kampala route in June 2026. [Seacom says traffic moves inland from the Mombasa landing stations](<https://seacom.co.ke/news/seacom-deploys-a-new-high-capacity-nairobikampala-route-to-strengthen-east-africas-digital-backbone>). No source names separate landing stations for any two cables. Operating would need two routes that share no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[Orange Liberia's chairman said its fibre link to Cote d'Ivoire let Liberia keep 100% of its international internet traffic](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/orange-liberia-celebrates-completion-of-ace-fiber-rerouting/article_7e13b2a8-da30-46a6-8b9b-68f96d819ff1.html>), during a four-day ACE cable outage. [The LTA chairman said a second landing at Buchanan is sought but not yet built](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/liberia-on-the-verge-of-5g-revolution/article_992b027e-4c8a-4578-bf70-baf2e2eabeeb.html>). In the last twelve months, [TechAfrica News reported Liberian officials saying the country depends on a single international route, the ACE submarine cable](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/16/liberia-advances-regional-fiber-optic-expansion-strategy-through-transco-clsg-partnership/>). It lands at one point in Monrovia. No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic.

[The Medusa submarine cable, 8,700 km and linking Libya to Mediterranean countries, was inaugurated on 10 May 2025 at Misrata](<https://libyaherald.com/2025/05/medusa-submarine-cable-project-linking-libya-with-europe-inaugurated>), according to the state holding company LPTIC. [Libya United International Company signed the connection contract in November 2023](<https://libyaherald.com/2025/05/medusa-submarine-cable-project-linking-libya-with-europe-inaugurated>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a second international fibre route in service. Nothing has been found saying other operators buy capacity on this route, or that it runs on open-access or wholesale terms. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[In November 2026 Capacity said Lesotho has no cable landing of its own](<https://capacityglobal.com/news/above-1000m-can-starlink-resellers-solve-lesothos-connectivity-problem/>). It said the country's international traffic reaches global networks over links across the border into South Africa. [The regulator's sector review, on data collected in August 2016, found Lesotho's operators drew international bandwidth from the WACS, EASSy and SEACOM cables](<https://lca.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/filr/2334/Final%20Integrated%20Report%2013022018.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says Lesotho's routes run through a neighbour other than South Africa. Operating would need two routes that share no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[The Conversation said in August 2026 that Morocco is connected to about ten submarine cables](<https://theconversation.com/le-maroc-futur-leader-continental-africain-des-data-centers-et-de-lia-288658>), Africa-1 and 2Africa among them. In the last twelve months, [Orange Maroc announced the landing of the Medusa cable at Nador on 16 December 2025](<https://lematin.ma/economie/orange-maroc-accueille-le-cable-dinterconnectivite-sous-marin-medusa/319447>). Le Matin describes the station as the first open-access cable landing station in the kingdom. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes sharing no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[Madagascar is linked by four submarine cables, Madagascar Newsroom said in December 2024](<https://www.madagascarnewsroom.com/2024/12/madagascar-cables-sous-marins--t4.html>): Lion 1 and 2, EASSy, METISS and 2Africa. EASSy lands at Toliara in the south-west, METISS at Fort Dauphin in the south-east and 2Africa at Mahajanga in the north-west. [Telma said in February 2023 that EASSy, LION and METISS reach the country through its national backbone](<https://www.axian-telecom.com/ac-content/uploads/2023/02/AXIAN-Telecom-Press-release-2Africa-landing-in-Madagascar-VA.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says other operators buy capacity at the landing station or on the cable. Mature would need other operators buying capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[Afribone Mali says its international links run over optical fibre through Dakar and Abidjan to the ACE and MainOne submarine cables](<https://afribone.com/a-propos/>). In the last twelve months, [the national fibre backbones of Mali and Senegal were interconnected and inaugurated on 5 October 2026 at Kidira-Diboli](<https://gouvernement.ml/cooperation-numerique-et-technologique-les-backbones-du-mali-et-du-senegal-sinterconnectent/>), the Malian government portal said. [Agence Ecofin says the link gives landlocked Mali a route to the 2Africa, ACE and SAT-3 cables landing in Senegal](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0810-142240-le-mali-ouvre-une-nouvelle-route-vers-l-internet-mondial-par-le-senegal>). It describes the link as an additional corridor to an existing terrestrial axis. No source found says other operators buy capacity on these routes. Mature would need other operators buying capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[2Africa lands at Maputo and Nacala, while EASSy and SEACOM both land at Maputo](<https://www.submarinenetworks.com/en/systems/asia-europe-africa/2africa/wiocc-and-tmcel-partner-to-boost-2africa-connectivity-in-mozambique>), Submarine Networks said in July 2025. [Vodacom Mozambique says it built the landing station at Nacala](<https://www.diarioeconomico.co.mz/2025/11/21/trends/inovacao/ceo-talks-queremos-garantir-95-de-cobertura-de-rede-ate-2030-simon-karikari/>), with direct links to Europe and the Americas. [The research network MoRENet had 60 Gbps abroad by October 2025](<https://africarxiv.ubuntunet.net/bitstreams/9427cb02-feef-4b3f-b03b-84cb4efea3cb/download>), over two routes. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [WIOCC agreed on 23 July 2025 to deliver capacity on 2Africa East to the operator Tmcel](<https://www.submarinenetworks.com/en/systems/asia-europe-africa/2africa/wiocc-and-tmcel-partner-to-boost-2africa-connectivity-in-mozambique>), which is not the cable's owner.

[Mauritania has been connected to the ACE cable since 2011 and still depends on it](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0505-138141-internet-la-mauritanie-amorce-le-deploiement-de-son-deuxieme-cable-sous-marin>), with no fully operational alternative, Ecofin said in May 2026. In the last twelve months, [a second cable began coastal installation on 4 May 2026, with service expected in January 2027](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0505-55269-mauritania-expands-internet-capacity-with-new-undersea-cable-project>). [On 1 May 2026 Moov Mauritel said it had put the West Africa cable into operation](<https://nouakchott24.info/node/14732>). Ecofin's report four days later still describes ACE as the single system. No source found names a second international fibre route fully in service. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[Mauritius had five submarine fibre cables, Defimedia said in May 2024](<https://defimedia.info/internet-et-telecommunications-un-nouveau-cable-sous-marin-de-fibre-optique-pour-remplacer-le-safe>): SAFE, LION, EASSy, METISS and MARS. [Mauritius Telecom had put a sixth, T3, into operation days earlier](<https://defimedia.info/internet-et-telecommunications-un-nouveau-cable-sous-marin-de-fibre-optique-pour-remplacer-le-safe>). [Telecom Review Africa listed four systems in July 2025](<https://www.telecomreviewafrica.com/articles/features/12397-sublime-seas-to-storage-sphere-mauritius-expands-hyperscale-data-hub/>): SAFE, LION, LION2 and METISS. [Mauritius Telecom's chief executive counted five cables in February 2026](<https://lexpress.mu/node/554669>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes sharing no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[Airtel Malawi says it has increased its international connectivity from three to five fibre routes](<https://www.maraviexpress.com/airtel-malawi-plc-brings-new-era-of-digital-connectivity-with-volte-and-5g-services/>). [It says these include new links through Tanzania and through Mozambique via Nacala](<https://www.maraviexpress.com/airtel-malawi-plc-brings-new-era-of-digital-connectivity-with-volte-and-5g-services/>). [TNM says it acquired additional fibre routes into Malawi via Zambia and Mozambique](<https://malawi24.com/2024/05/21/tnm-invests-mk4-billion-restores-internet-disrupted-by-sea-cable-cuts/>), after subsea cable cuts left it only the Mchinji/Chipata link. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic.

[Telecom Namibia says WACS has served since 2011 and Equiano landed on 1 July 2022](<https://telecom.na/media-centre/650-telecom-namibia-to-leverage-the-potential-for-digital-transformation-of-the-namibian-economy-%E2%80%93-a-reply-to-the-world-bank-group-report>), both at Swakopmund. [It activated capacity on Equiano at its new cable station on 31 July 2024](<https://www.telecom.na/media-centre/797-telecom-namibia-celebrates-32-years-with-historic-inauguration-of-the-%E2%80%9Ctelecom-namibia-equiano-cable-station%E2%80%9D-and-activation-of-capacity-on-equiano-subsea-cable>). In the last twelve months, [Paratus called its Trans-Kalahari fibre route from Windhoek to Johannesburg another route out of the country in October 2026](<https://paratus.africa/namibia/news/paratus-namibia-continues-to-reshape-the-connectivity-landscape/>), with onward access to east coast cables such as SEACOM. [On 12 June 2026 Telecom Namibia agreed to give Angola Telecom 1 Tbps of dedicated capacity on Equiano](<https://telecom.na/media-centre/910-telecom-namibia,-angola-telecom,-and-satcab-sign-landmark-sarssy-and-equiano-submarine-cable-systems-master-service-agreement-in-angola>). It will also host Angola Telecom's equipment at its landing station.

[Maroc Telecom's 5,700 km transafrican terrestrial cable runs from Morocco to Niger via Mauritania, Mali and Burkina Faso, and is recorded as completed in 2022](<https://leseco.ma/business/maroc-telecom-plus-de-454-mmdh-investis-en-afrique.html>). It lets Moov Africa Niger reach international bandwidth. In the last twelve months, [the ministers of Niger and Algeria presided on 6 October 2026 at Assamaka over the official launch of operation of the trans-Saharan fibre backbone](<https://anp.ne/niger-algerie-lancement-a-assamaka-de-lexploitation-de-la-dorsale-transsaharienne-a-fibre-optique/>), which links Niger to Algeria. The report gives no capacity. It does not say Niger's traffic runs over it. No source found names a second international fibre route in service. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service.

[Nigeria's cables land at two stations: most at Lagos, and 2Africa at Qua Iboe, the first landing outside Lagos](<https://techcabal.com/2026/02/09/equinix-opens-first-south-south-data-centre/>). [TechCabal states Nigeria has eight active subsea cable systems, with combined design capacity of about 370 Tbps](<https://techcabal.com/2026/09/14/mtn-controls-55-of-nigerias-tiny-fibre-market/>). [Equinix and MainOne provide the 2Africa landing facilities, middle-mile fibre and carrier-neutral data centre PR1](<https://techcabal.com/2026/02/09/equinix-opens-first-south-south-data-centre/>), for network operators, cloud providers and enterprises. In the last twelve months, [MainOne activated a multi-gigabit connection at Victor Attah airport, Uyo, on 8 August 2026](<https://africanpilot.africa/akwa-ibom-victor-attah-internet/>).

[Rwanda has three international fibre routes to the SEACOM cable, through Tanzania and Kenya](<https://aipi.rw/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/IT-INVESTOR-GUIDEBOOK.pdf>), the investment board's guidebook said in March 2024. [The Internet Society lists land links to Burundi, the DR Congo, Tanzania and Uganda](<https://www.internetsociety.org/resources/doc/2024/2024-east-africa-submarine-cable-outage-report/>), and no submarine cable. In the last twelve months, [Paratus switched on its 2,000 km fibre from Mombasa to Goma in February 2026](<https://itweb.africa/article/paratus-lights-up-new-east-africa-fibre-highway-linking-goma-to-mombasa/wbrpOqg2aJQMDLZn>), through Nairobi, Kampala and Kigali. It carries traffic for its first wholesale customers. No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry the country's traffic.

[Sudan has land fibre links to Ethiopia, Egypt, South Sudan and Chad](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/blog/2024/03/chads-recent-outages-highlight-resiliency-gaps/>), beside submarine cables at Port Sudan, the Internet Society said in March 2024. [A 1 Gbps undersea link for aid agencies opened at Port Sudan in August 2024](<https://www.etcluster.org/blog/undersea-cable-delivers-critical-connectivity-sudan>), built with Sudatel. In the last twelve months, [DCD said in February 2026 that Port Sudan connects several cables to the Middle East and Europe](<https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/ethio-telecom-djibouti-telecom-and-sudatel-group-sign-strategic-fiber-agreement/>). It named none of them. [Djibouti Telecom's chief executive said at a signing on 4 February 2026 that cables run between Port Sudan and Jeddah](<https://www.lanation.dj/djibouti-telecom-ethio-telecomet-sudatel-telecom-group-signent-un-accord-strategique-pour-linitiative-horizon-fiber/>). No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable, such as 2Africa or Equiano, to carry it.

[ACE, MainOne, SAT-3, SHARE and 2Africa were named in January 2025 among the submarine cables landing in Dakar](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/data-centers/paix-to-build-data-center-in-senegal>). [In May 2025 Phase 3 Telecom and Sonatel activated a 3,500 km land route from Lagos to Dakar](<https://www.phase3telecom.com/phase-3-and-sonatel-unveils-3500km-terrestrial-fibre-route/>), through Benin, Togo and Ghana. In the last twelve months, [Sonatel said 2Africa entered service at its Senegal landing station in December 2025](<https://sonatel.sn/sonatel-annonce-la-mise-en-service-du-cable-sous-marin-2africa-le-plus-performant-jamais-deploye-en-afrique/>), with a nominal capacity of 180 Tbit/s. Onix runs a carrier-neutral data centre at that station. In 2023 it said the centre [gives companies direct access to several subsea cables and backhaul routes](<https://onixdatacentres.com/2023/05/11/tier-3-facility-in-dakar-2023-completion/>) on carrier-neutral terms.

[The ACE cable has served Sierra Leone since 15 December 2012, landing at Freetown](<https://ace-submarinecable.com/en/submarine-cable/>). [In 2024 The Conversation said only one fibre cable comes into the country](<https://theconversation.com/undersea-cables-for-africas-internet-retrace-history-225912>). [In June 2024 ECOWAS said the six countries of its Amilcar Cabral cable project, Sierra Leone among them, each have one landing station](<https://www.ecowas.int/4th-meeting-of-the-ecowas-ministerial-steering-committee-for-the-amilcar-cabral-submarine-telecom-cable-project/>). In the last twelve months, [the government announced in November 2026 a National Cable Consortium to land a second cable, a 45 million dollar project](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/11/18/sierra-leone-announces-45-million-second-submarine-cable-project/>). It is planned, not in service. No source found names a land route through a neighbour. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[DatacenterDynamics lists Somalia's current landings as DARE1 at Mogadishu and Bosaso and Gulf2Africa at Bosaso and Berbera](<https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/hormuud-telecom-cable-landing-station-construction-completed-in-somalia/>). Two cables therefore land at different stations. The same source reports that Hormuud Telecom's newly completed Somali cable landing station is open-access and will accommodate various submarine cables. In the last twelve months, [The Star reported that Somcable Submarine Network operates two international subsea landings, 2Africa and PEACE, at the Port of Berbera](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/2026-09-14-kenyas-digital-future-takes-shape-as-data-giants-converge-in-nairobi>). Its chief technology officer calls them two physically diverse routes.

[South Sudan has no submarine cable landing of its own and depends on land fibre links to its neighbours](<https://dig.watch/countries/south-sudan>). [In August 2025 ITWeb Africa reported that it still had only one fibre connection, a 200 km line from Uganda to Juba](<https://itweb.africa/article/south-sudan-to-lay-fibre-from-kenya/lwrKx73Y94lqmg1o>), with links from Kenya and Djibouti only planned. In the last twelve months, [the regulator set up a committee to oversee the international gateway in January 2026](<https://www.eyeradio.org/nca-establishes-gateway-and-data-center-oversight-committee>). [A World Bank plan of August 2026 names a land link across the border with Kenya](<https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099082026093524598>). No source found names a second international fibre route in service. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[The World Bank records that the ACE submarine cable landed in Sao Tome and Principe in November 2011](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/234391468190440376/txt/ICR3141-P117652-Box391488B-OUO-9.txt>), and that it was commercially launched in February 2013. [The ACE consortium states the 17,000 km cable entered service on 15 December 2012](<https://ace-submarinecable.com/en/submarine-cable/>). It lists a landing station at Sao Tome and Principe, where ACE is the first international submarine cable to land. [The World Bank says the country's participation was on an open-access basis through STP-Cabo SARL](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/234391468190440376/txt/ICR3141-P117652-Box391488B-OUO-9.txt>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a second international fibre route in service. Establishing would need a second international fibre route in service, even one sharing a landing station or a neighbour with the first.

[UASF states that EPTC's connectivity relied on an upstream provider in South Africa through its North, West and South routes](<https://uasf.esccom.org.sz/programmes/connectivity-programmes/>). [ESCCOM's investigation confirmed that Jenny Internet Eswatini used a direct cross-border fibre link at the Malutha Border Post](<https://esccom.org.sz/publications/notices/docs/EPTC%20AND%20JENNY%20FINAL%20%20DECISION%20Notice%205.pdf>), which bypassed EPTC's backbone. In the last twelve months, the Commission ordered Jenny to use EPTC backbone connectivity from 1 July 2026. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes sharing no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity.

[Seychelles Cable Systems says PEACE is Seychelles' second submarine fibre cable landing, in service from 16 November 2022](<https://www.nation.sc/articles/16417/seychelles-achieves-security-in-international-connectivity-peace-operational-in-seychelles>). It says PEACE runs alongside the SEAS cable commissioned over ten years earlier. [The World Bank project information document says Seychelles has three submarine cables](<http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099100726053521931>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The source does not name the SEAS landing station. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations. Operating would need two routes sharing no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[Russell Southwood wrote in November 2026 that Chad has two routes to the Camtel landing station at Kribi](<https://russellsouthwood.substack.com/p/chad-living-in-a-landlocked-dangerous>), with a third planned. [In March 2026 Chad told ITU-D that a 35 km fibre link to Cameroon is its only operational link](<https://www.itu.int/md/D26-SG01-C-0040/en>). [Chad's telecoms minister said in October 2026 that only one international access, through Cameroon, is active](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/tchad-le-plan-de-connexion-au-reseau-internet-mondial-presente-au-gaids-a-seoul/>). In the last twelve months, [the minister told the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in November 2026 that three links with Cameroon and Sudan are completed](<https://pp.itu.int/2026/en/itu_policy_statements/chad/>). No source found says a route that avoids Cameroon is in service. Operating would need two routes sharing no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity.

[Lomé Data Centre states its own direct access to four submarine cables, ACE, 2Africa, WACS and Equiano](<https://lomedatacentre.tg/en/n-home-page-en/>), on a page dated 24 September 2025. [Data Landscapers lists one cable landing station for CSquared, for the Equiano cable at Lomé](<https://data-landscapers.com/2026/06/11/sovereign-infrastructure/>). In the last twelve months, [Mobile Europe reported on 15 July 2026 that CSquared's architecture includes Equiano, landing in Nigeria and Togo](<https://www.mobileeurope.co.uk/csquared-boosts-internet-resilence-integrating-with-2africa-west/>). It says the system reaches Benin, Ghana and Burkina Faso by terrestrial backbone. No source found says two of the routes land at different stations, or run through two different neighbours. Operating would need two routes sharing no landing station, and a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carrying the country's traffic.

[The US ITA commercial guide says Tunisie Telecom, the leading international connectivity provider, manages three sub-sea cables](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/tunisia-telecommunications-equipment-services>). [INT decision 165/2013 orders the national operator to offer alternative operators regulated, cost-oriented access to international capacity](<https://intt.tn/upload/txts/fr/d%C3%A9cision_165_cables_sm.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [Orange Tunisie announced on 24 June 2026 that MEDUSA is in operational service via the Bizerte landing station](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/06/24/le-cable-medusa-desormais-operationnel-la-tunisie-renforce-sa-connectivite-internationale/>). [It says MEDUSA carries its first international traffic and has four fibre pairs of 24 Tbps each](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/06/24/le-cable-medusa-desormais-operationnel-la-tunisie-renforce-sa-connectivite-internationale/>). [Medusa describes its system as carrier-neutral](<https://medusascs.com/news/medusa-submarine-cable-system-lands-in-bizerte/>).

[In June 2025 the ministry said three submarine cables are active: SEACOM, EASSy and 2Africa](<https://www.itu.int/net/wsis/review/inc/docs/reports/country/Tanzania__20YearCountryReport_WSISOutcomes.pdf>). They [land in Dar es Salaam](<https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/business/wingu-africa-now-targets-tanzania-as-region-s-digital-hub-5441614>). [In July 2025 the minister said the Horohoro route with Kenya gives Tanzania a land path to eight undersea cables through Kenya](<https://dailynews.co.tz/new-fibre-link-to-boost-east-africas-digital-resilience/>). In the last twelve months, [a minister counted four submarine cable stations in July 2026](<https://www.mawasiliano.go.tz/news/tanzania-yaonesha-mafanikio-ya-utekelezaji-wa-akili-unde-ai-katika-mkutano-wa-kimataifa-wa-waico-2026>), without naming them. No source found says other operators buy capacity at the landing station or on the cables. Mature would need other operators buying capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

[Xalam Analytics wrote in July 2025 that Uganda's few routes abroad run mainly over the Seacom and EASSY cables, through Tanzania and Kenya](<https://cms.d4dhub.eu/assets/Initiatives/Data-Governance-in-Africa/Digital-Investment-Facility/2507_Country-Market-Briefs/Data-Center-Market-Brief-Uganda.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [Seacom opened a Nairobi-Kisumu-Kampala route on 17 June 2026, with 1 Tbps lit](<https://seacom.co.ke/news/seacom-deploys-a-new-high-capacity-nairobikampala-route-to-strengthen-east-africas-digital-backbone>). [Paratus switched on its 2,000 km G2M route from Mombasa through Nairobi and Kampala to Goma in February 2026](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/fiber-networking/paratus-lights-up-new-east-africa-fiber-route>). [ITWeb Africa reported in September 2026 that Liquid had added a third route from Mombasa to the Uganda border](<https://www.itweb.africa/article/interview-liquid-targets-africas-data-centre-gap/xA9POvNE2Gxqo4J8>). No source found says a cable of more than 100 Tbps design capacity carries the country's traffic. Operating would need such a cable to carry the country's traffic.

[The Conversation Africa says southern Africa's internet comes largely through two landing stations in South Africa](<https://theconversation.com/undersea-cables-for-africas-internet-retrace-history-225912>), at Melkbosstrand near Cape Town and Mtunzini in northern KwaZulu-Natal. [Bayobab says 2Africa West is open for business with South African landings at Yzerfontein and Duynefontein](<https://bayobab.africa/2africa-west-seamless-connectivity-at-scale/>). [Teraco states its Cape Town campus is connected to all subsea cable systems landing in the Cape region](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/11/10/teraco-expands-cape-town-ct2-data-centre-to-50mw-boosting-africas-hyperscale-capacity/>): ACE, Equiano, SAT-3, SAFE, WACS and 2Africa. [Xalam Analytics states South Africa's wholesale fibre regulatory regime is the most open in Africa](<https://cms.d4dhub.eu/assets/Initiatives/Data-Governance-in-Africa/Digital-Investment-Facility/Data-Center-Market-Briefs-South-Africa-2026.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months.

[Zambia has fibre links to eight neighbouring countries](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/zambia-and-mozambique-launch-fibre-optic-interconnector/>), its technology minister, Felix Mutati, said in February 2026. In the last twelve months, [Bayobab and Vodacom Mocambique opened a fibre interconnection at the Zambia-Mozambique border on 21 February 2026](<https://bayobab.africa/bayobab-zambia-and-vodacom-mocambique-launch-strategic-fibre-interconnection-at-zambia-mozambique-border/>). It gives Zambia a route to subsea cables on the Indian Ocean coast, including direct connectivity to 2Africa. No source found says other operators buy capacity at the landing station or on the cable. Mature would need other operators buying capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or the cable on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.
